sources.entry: mcp - The official Python SDK for building Model Context Protocol servers and clients.

summary.one_liner: The official Python SDK for building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and clients, letting LLM applications access tools, resources, and prompts.
summary.what_it_does: The package provides an MCP server framework where plain type-hinted Python functions decorated with @mcp.tool() or @mcp.resource() become MCP tools and templated resources, with schemas derived from the type hints. It also includes an MCP client (the Client class) that connects to remote servers over Streamable HTTP, or launches a local server as a stdio subprocess, or uses a custom transport. An optional cli extra adds the mcp command with subcommands dev (MCP Inspector), run, and install. The README says it supports the stdio, Streamable HTTP, and SSE transports. Full documentation (Get started guide, What's new in v2, API reference, migration guide) is hosted externally.
use_cases: build an MCP server exposing tools to an LLM app
expose data as MCP resources with URI templates
write a Python client that calls tools on an MCP server
test an MCP server in the MCP Inspector
run an MCP server over Streamable HTTP
connect to a local MCP server via stdio subprocess
how_to_run: Create server.py with an MCPServer and @mcp.tool()/@mcp.resource() functions
uv run mcp dev server.py  # open in MCP Inspector
uv run mcp run server.py --transport streamable-http
Use `async with Client(url) as client:` and client.call_tool(...) to call the server
notable: Type hints and docstrings define tool schemas automatically, with no hand-written JSON Schema
Single package provides both server and client APIs
Supports stdio, Streamable HTTP, and SSE transports
Official SDK maintained under the modelcontextprotocol organization
caveats: Detailed documentation is external; the README itself is a brief overview
The CLI tooling requires the optional cli extra
keywords: let llm call my python functions
connect llm app to data source
